task: Visually upgrade the town's buildings in the 3D ESL town-builder so the streets read as a charming toy Japanese town rather than coloured boxes. The generic houses and shops are the priority; the hand-built landmarks get a lighter consistency pass.
notes: PROJECT: Vite + three.js, no framework. A 3D town an elementary-school class builds by speaking English. Art direction is deliberately 'toy town': chunky low-poly shapes, flat cheerful colours, MeshLambertMaterial under a hemisphere + directional light. That direction is correct and must be preserved - this task is about adding CHARM AND DETAIL within it, not changing the style, not going realistic, not adding PBR/textures.

CURRENT SURVEY SCREENSHOTS are in qa-evidence/survey/*.png (town-overview, houses-street, houses-close, shops-street, landmark-school, landmark-bakery, landmark-hospital, landmark-library, landmark-station, landmark-park). Look at them first - they are the evidence behind every fault listed below. Regenerate them any time with: npm run dev -- --port 5199, then node .ai/capture-building-survey.mjs 5199 qa-evidence/survey

FAULT 1 - houses and shops are detailed on ONE face only. makeHouse() in src/world/props.js puts its windows and door on the +z face and nothing anywhere else, so from the other three sides every house is a blank cube. In qa-evidence/survey/houses-close.png a house fills half the frame as one featureless tan wall. The town camera orbits freely, so every facade is seen.

FAULT 2 - the wall palette collapses to beige. HOUSE_WALLS offers six colours but the town reads as an unbroken field of sand/cream (see town-overview.png); only the roofs carry colour. Houses should be individually recognisable from the air.

FAULT 3 - buildings have no ground contact. They meet the grass at a hard edge with no plinth, foundation, path to the door, step, hedge, gate or planting, so they look pasted onto the lawn rather than built on it.
FAULT 4 - roofs are bare prisms. The gable/hip roofs have no ridge cap, no fascia band and no eave overhang detail, so the roofline is a flat silhouette.

FAULT 5 - shops are a single flat storey: box + coloured band + glass strip + awning, with no door, no upper-floor windows, no vertical Japanese-style sign, and no street clutter (crates, a parked bike, planters, an A-board). The coloured roof band reads as a solid saturated plate (see the purple RAMEN roof in town-overview.png).

FAULT 6 - a faint diagonal cross-hatch striping is visible across large flat walls built from roundedBox(); it is the RoundedBoxGeometry triangulation catching the Lambert light on big panels. Visible on the tan wall in houses-close.png. Fix or avoid it on large surfaces.

THE LANDMARKS (src/buildings/procedural.js and src/buildings/extras.js) are already hand-tuned and mostly good - the school and hospital have storey bands, window grids, signage and canopies. Do NOT redesign them. Give them only a light consistency pass so they share whatever new ground-contact and roofline language the houses and shops get, and fix anything that is clearly broken or bare on a face.

PERFORMANCE IS A HARD CONSTRAINT: this runs on Japanese elementary-school Chromebooks with integrated GPUs. src/core/materials.js caches every material and geometry precisely so the renderer can batch. Reuse mat()/box()/roundedBox()/cylinder() from that module; do not create per-instance materials, do not switch to MeshStandardMaterial, and keep the added mesh count per building modest. The town builds ~45 houses plus shops at once.
Record the visual direction you settle on in DESIGN_DECISIONS.md and update CURRENT_STATE.md.
Read DESIGN_DECISIONS.md before changing the look - it carries the existing art-direction rationale, and recording this pass's decision there is part of the task.

After you have settled the visual approach, you may delegate bounded mechanical sub-work to a lower-cost worker rather than doing it yourself. Write a work order as JSON (task, requirements, constraints, startingPoints, validation, plus complexity / bounded / exploration / risk / expectedCost) and run: node ~/.claude/workers/bin/delegate.js <order.json> --controller codex --json. The router decides whether a cheaper worker is available and affordable; if it routes back to you, just do the work. Inspect the resulting diff and validation output yourself before continuing. Keep the visual judgment, the shared material/geometry design and anything coupled in your own hands. Never call another worker directly; the router is the only path down.
requirements: Every generic house and shop looks finished from all four sides - windows, and where sensible a door, balcony, vent, downpipe, meter box or utility detail, on more than the front face. No blank walls at street scale.

Houses read as individually distinct in a street and from the overhead view: wall colour actually varies across the palette instead of collapsing to beige, and silhouettes vary (storeys, roof type, porch/entry, small annexe or garage).
Buildings sit convincingly on the ground: a plinth/foundation edge, and an approach - path, step, low wall, hedge or planting - between the building and the grass.
Rooflines carry detail: an eave/fascia band, a ridge cap or equivalent, so the roof is not a single untextured prism.

Shops gain depth: an actual entrance, a second storey or parapet where the height allows, a vertical or projecting sign in the Japanese shopping-street idiom, and a little street-level clutter so the shop front feels inhabited.
The diagonal shading striping on large roundedBox walls is gone.
Landmarks in src/buildings/ share the new ground-contact and roofline language without being redesigned.
Style unchanged: chunky low-poly toy town, flat cheerful colours, MeshLambertMaterial. Nothing photoreal, no imported models, no new texture assets.
makeHouse(rng) and makeShop(rng, label) keep their existing signatures and keep setting userData.footprint, which scenery placement and collision depend on.
constraints: Do not reintroduce the Kenney suburban .glb houses. src/world/houseModels.js and public/assets/buildings/ were deliberately deleted this session; houses are procedural again on purpose.
Do not create per-building materials or geometries - go through the caches in src/core/materials.js.
Do not switch away from MeshLambertMaterial or add MeshStandardMaterial/PBR.
Do not add downloaded 3D models, image textures or new asset files.
Do not change town layout, lot positions, the road graph, pedestrian or vehicle systems, or src/config/town.js.
Do not grow a building's footprint beyond what makeHouse/makeShop already produce - lots and sidewalk clearance were tuned by hand and buildings must not spill onto the sidewalk.
Do not touch src/world/characterModels.js, src/world/characters.js or src/systems/pedestrians.js.
Keep the per-frame cost flat: no new per-frame CPU work, no new lights, no shadow-map changes.
validation: npm run dev -- --port 5199 then node .ai/capture-building-survey.mjs 5199 qa-evidence/survey-after - capture the same ten shots after the change and compare them against qa-evidence/survey/
node .ai/audit-landmark-extents.mjs http://localhost:5199 - no landmark may newly spill past its plot
Zero page errors in the capture run (the harness prints the count)
